discussion_comments.comment_body:
**#4 Medium (CONFIRMED): hard exit regresses working read-only deployments.**

A deployment mounting APP_DIR read-only (e.g. `-v ./data:/app/data:ro` with a pre-existing `logs/` subdir) and keeping config/logs in Postgres booted fine before this PR: the old script's chown failure was warn-and-continue, `mkdir -p` on the existing `logs/` was a no-op, and the Go server never writes to APP_DIR when explicit store config is present (`initStores` in `transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go` only creates `config.db`/`logs.db` when store config is absent; `os.MkdirAll` on an existing dir succeeds regardless of writability). After this PR the writability probe fails and the container crash-loops before the app starts.

Suggested: an escape hatch such as `BIFROST_SKIP_WRITE_CHECK=1` that downgrades this `exit 1` to the old warning, so external-store deployments with intentionally read-only data dirs keep working.

(Helm and the Terraform ECS/ACI modules are unaffected: helm mounts no data volume in postgres mode, and the terraform entrypoints write `config.json` into `/app/data` before this script runs.)
